newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China border police alert to safeguard HK handover.
newsitem.headline: China border police alert to safeguard HK handover.

text.p: Police in the south China frontier city of Shenzhen are on high alert to prevent illegal migrants sneaking into Hong Kong for the British colony's July 1 return to China, a Hong Kong newspaper said.
The Chinese-language Ming Pao newspaper quoted sources on Monday as saying some 40,000 Shenzhen police had stepped up border patrols to ensure a smooth handover of power here.
The newspaper said security officials were also considering blocking all roads leading to the Hong Kong-China border on June 30.
Neither China nor Britain wants an influx of mainland Chinese into crowded Hong Kong. The border stays even after the territory becomes a Special region of China.
As the historic changeover is a focus of world attention, Beijing is concerned about security in Hong Kong, a British colony for 156 years which reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.

China has pledged that capitalist Hong Kong's 6.4 million population will keep its way of life unchanged for 50 years. Mainland Chinese will not be allowed to enter the territory freely to prevent any risk of destabilising Hong Kong.
But smugglers have fabricated rumours that Hong Kong will grant amnesty to illegal immigrants after July 1.
Thousands of mainland Chinese want to go to Hong Kong where living standards are much higher than in China.
